name: Barbaresco

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, hot summer

climate: Nebbiolo sits in its sweet spot, so the wines can show the style it is known for.

terms: Denominazione di Origine Controllata e Garantita, Italy's top tier. Stricter than DOC, and given only to wines that have been DOC for at least seven years.
keyfacts: Barbaresco must age at least 26 months from 1 November of the harvest year, 9 of them in wood, and Riserva at least 50 months.
The minimum alcohol level is 12.5 per cent.
The Barbaresco Consorzio introduced Menzioni Geografiche Aggiuntive (MGA) subzones in 2007, and the final number of subzones is 66.

notes: It smells of roses or violets, with cherry, truffle, fennel and licorice, and turns smoky, earthy and leathery with age.
It is very tannic and tight when young and is usually best 5 to 10 years after the vintage.
Its tannins soften sooner than Barolo's, so it is more approachable young but usually ages less long.

blurb.text: A red wine made from Nebbiolo in the Langhe, just east of Alba in Piedmont, from Barbaresco, Neive, Treiso and part of Alba. A DOC since 1966 and a DOCG since 1980, it is often compared with Barolo.
